name: Manchester
meta_description: Manchester brewery tours, craft beer tastings and historic pub walks — explore the Northern Quarter and beyond with top-rated guided experiences.
intro_md:
Manchester takes its beer seriously, and has done since the Victorians. The Northern Quarter is the obvious starting point — a dense grid of red-brick streets where craft beer bars sit alongside record shops and street art — while neighbouring Ancoats has grown into one of the city's best eating districts, with the restored Mackie Mayor market hall on Swan Street sitting handily between the two.

The city's pub heritage rewards a slow crawl. The Marble Arch on Rochdale Road pours beers from its own brewery beneath a gloriously tiled Victorian interior, and the Peveril of the Peak's green-glazed exterior makes it one of Manchester's most photographed pubs. In summer, the canalside pubs of Castlefield are a fine alternative.

Don't miss:

- The Northern Quarter's craft beer bars
- Mackie Mayor food hall on Swan Street
- The Marble Arch's tiled Victorian interior
- Canalside pints in Castlefield

gyg_tours.title: Manchester: Craft Beer Tasting in the Northern Quarter
gyg_tours.summary: A seated, guided tasting of five craft beers in Manchester's Northern Quarter, with an expert host covering tasting technique and beer styles.
gyg_tours.description_md:
This 90-minute guided tasting masterclass explores Manchester's independent craft beer culture in the Northern Quarter. In a relaxed, seated venue with small groups of up to 10 people, you sample five modern craft beers while a knowledgeable host explains professional tasting techniques, brewing methods, ingredients and flavour profiles. It is designed for anyone curious about modern beer styles, from first-time tasters to seasoned enthusiasts.</description_md>
<parameter name="meeting_point">Outside 16 Tariff St, Manchester M1 2FN
highlights: Taste five modern craft beer styles
Learn professional beer tasting techniques
Explore Manchester's independent craft beer scene
Each beer served as a 1/3 pint pour
Small groups of up to 10 people
Learn about brewing methods and flavour profiles

gyg_tours.title: Manchester: Pub Tour
gyg_tours.summary: A two-hour guided tour of Manchester city-centre pubs exploring the city's drinking history and pub culture, finishing with a short pub quiz.
gyg_tours.description_md: This guided walking tour explores Manchester's pub culture and drinking history, visiting a selection of classic pubs around the city centre. Along the way, your guide shares the origins of common drinking phrases, the stories behind pub names, and tales of notable figures linked to the venues. The tour runs for around two hours and ends with a lighthearted pub quiz with prizes.
highlights: Visit classic Manchester city-centre pubs
Learn the history of Manchester's drinking culture
Discover the origins of drinking phrases and pub names
Hear stories of notable local figures
End with a pub quiz and prizes
Two-hour guided tour in English
gyg_tours.meeting_point: Outside Central Library, St Peter's Square, Manchester, M2 5PD

gyg_tours.title: Manchester: Guided Walking Tour of Historic Pubs & City
gyg_tours.summary: A guided walk through Manchester's historic pubs, including the Old Wellington and Sinclair's Oyster Bar, run by a social enterprise whose guides have experienced homelessness.
gyg_tours.description_md: A two-hour guided walking tour through Manchester's historic public houses, led by a guide from the social enterprise Invisible Cities. As you visit a selection of the city's most storied pubs, including the Old Wellington and Sinclair's Oyster Bar, your guide shares tales linking these venues to Manchester's music, football, and social history. The route explores how the city has changed over time while raising awareness of homelessness.
highlights: Explore historic Manchester pubs on foot
Visit the Old Wellington and Sinclair's Oyster Bar
Stories of music, football and social change
Guided by a local from Invisible Cities
Supports a social enterprise for former rough sleepers
gyg_tours.meeting_point: Main entrance of Manchester Cathedral; look for Andy in a green hoodie by the cathedral doors. Tour ends near Oxford Road Station.

gyg_tours.title: Manchester & Salford: Guided Food and Drink Walking Tour
gyg_tours.summary: A 3.5-hour walking tour spanning Manchester and Salford, taking in historic pubs, markets and street food, with food tastings and two drinks included.
gyg_tours.description_md: Discover the culinary heritage of Manchester and Salford on a guided food and drink walking tour led by a local guide. Explore the two neighbouring cities and sample an eclectic blend of food and drink that reflects their shared history and vibrant cultures. Along the way, learn about the cities' past and meet local characters as you journey between them.
highlights: Guided by a knowledgeable local guide
Sample a blend of food and drink
Explore both Manchester and Salford
Learn about the cities' history
Meet local characters along the way
gyg_tours.meeting_point: The Bridgewater Hall, Manchester (tour concludes at 40-42 Deansgate, Manchester M3 1RH)

gyg_tours.title: Manchester: Beer Bike Tour with Drinks and Music
gyg_tours.summary: A 75-minute pedal-powered group bike ride through Manchester with beer or prosecco on board, music, and a sober captain doing the steering.
gyg_tours.description_md: Pedal your way through Manchester's streets aboard a group beer bike on this 75-minute ride for up to 13 people. Guests enjoy a selection of drinks together while a sober captain steers the bike safely through the city. A Bluetooth sound system lets the group play their own music, making it suited to celebrations or a fun day out with friends.
highlights: Pedal through Manchester's streets on a beer bike
Enjoy beer or prosecco with friends
Play your own music via Bluetooth sound system
Group ride for up to 13 people
Sober captain steers you safely
Great for celebrations or a fun day out
